images.prompt:
Use case: product-mockup.
Asset type: one image in a coordinated three-angle premium technology website product sequence.
Input images: both are identity references for the SAME CYMBA wired earbud. Preserve that product, materials, two champagne contact pads, curved soft fin, round brushed graphite outer faceplate with fine champagne rim, grey silicone eartip seated on the opposite side of the housing, small black optical window where visible, and the cable leaving the lower housing. These are not composition templates.
Primary request: photograph ONE of this EXACT earbud from a genuinely DIFFERENT CAMERA ANGLE, not a 2D rotation or crop of the reference.
Style: very high fidelity premium studio product photography. Matte graphite and silicone, fine radial metal brushing, restrained champagne details, natural physical reflections, soft neutral key light upper-left and subtle rim illumination. Show real dimensional depth and believable geometry.
Composition: landscape 3:2 canvas. Isolated earbud centered, filling roughly 70 percent of width and 76 percent of height, with generous clear margins all around. Entire earbud, fin and eartip must remain visible. A short length of attached black cable trails down toward lower-right, then out of frame. No external shadows or floor; genuinely transparent background with preserved clean alpha edges. Object must remain readable on a very dark charcoal website.
Constraints: same physical earbud identity, no redesign, no additional pads or extra fins, no duplicated earbud, no new controls, no logos/text/callouts/arrows, no people or ears, no stand, no checkerboard painted into the image, no sci-fi glow. Do not invent internal electronic components; keep the housing assembled.
This image focuses on STIMULATION CONTACTS: Camera is above and toward the inner/contact side, looking down approximately 35 degrees, orbiting around the reference by approximately 50 degrees. The curved fin and both champagne contact surfaces should face the camera clearly, as the visual centre of attention. The circular outer faceplate is largely edge-on, visibly receding on the left. The silicone tip is still attached to its nozzle on the right/rear and appears foreshortened. Make the contact wing's thickness and two separate contact surfaces especially clear. A distinct elevated view, not the familiar eye-level three-quarter angle.

Show silicone lip thickness and the short nozzle connection into the housing. The graphite housing and contact fin recede behind the tip to the right.
